$schema_note: Authored reconstruction programme. Structure records remain the scene source of truth; tools/generate_inferred_infill.py checks its generated parcel against this ledger.
confidence: moderate aggregate; interpretive per anonymous instance
roof_total_note: 665 → 662 ON 2026-08-27 (ticket T-0032, owner ruling of 2026-08-17: 'close it at 665 or 662 — either is close'). The authored spec put six roofs in family I3, civic and public-service. The town's civic roofs on 1835-07-01 are THREE — the log jail, the council house and the lighthouse, all committed named records — and the other three slots counted nothing: the court-house is fall 1835, the engine house was contracted on 30 December 1835, the custom house is 1846, the market house 1837, the town hall was never built, and the United States Land Office was a room in somebody's building on Lake Street. The enumeration is docs/RESEARCH/civic_public_buildings_1835.md and tools/measure_institutional_claims.py re-settles every line of it against this dataset on every run of the gate. The three come OFF the total rather than being re-typed into ordinary families, because re-typing would invent three buildings on the strength of an arithmetic artifact; 662 is inside this file's own defensible_range. The institutional_public row moved with it, from south 10 / west 1 / north 1 to the census of named institutional records — south 5 / west 1 / north 3 — which is what carries the south district target from 370 to 365 and the north from 150 to 152. Every other row is exactly as authored.

south.character: Commercial core along South Water and Lake, then mixed blocks with density falling rapidly southward.

west.character: Older irregular fabric at Wolf Point approaches: cabins, taverns, yards, work and river storage.

north.character: Scattered development around Kinzie properties and crossings, with substantial open ground.

fort.character: Ten principal roofs in the custom Fort Dearborn compound; stockade and props are outside this roof count.

district_group_overshoots.$note: T-0211. A (district, group) cell where the town already stands OVER its row. tools/reconcile_665.py clamps these with max(0, ...) and sheds the excess from whichever group has the most slack, so an overshoot used to look exactly like a row that was right — that is how T-0032's institutional fault survived. tools/audit_group_matrix.py --check now refuses an UNDECLARED overshoot, a declaration whose size no longer matches the dataset, and a declaration for a cell that has stopped overshooting. Declaring an overshoot does not bless it; it says the number has been read and priced. The price is in 1835_665_roof_programme.json under remaining.district_group_shed_from.

north.warehouses_freight.why: The row is under-authored against the north bank the research has since recorded, not the town over-built. Six of the seven are pre-existing records — kinzie_hunter_warehouse, the four north_bank_shed_dearborn_* sheds and brickyard_north_side — and the seventh, recon_1835_north_f1_022, arrived with the audited North Division infill on 2026-08-12. Correcting the row means moving six roofs out of another North row: that changes the district's composition and is an authoring decision about the target, not a clamp. Filed as T-0283.

north.institutional_public.why: T-0032 set this row to the census of NAMED institutional records — council_house, north_side_school_1833 and watkins_school_house — which is the right basis for a group whose members are enumerable. A fourth roof stands beside them: recon_1835_north_i2_015, a generated I2 dealt in with the North Division infill on 2026-08-12, two weeks before that correction. The cell reads 4 against 3 and the overshoot is exactly that generated roof. Removing an adopted record is a separate decision from correcting a row. Filed as T-0283.

protected_existing_policy: Every existing record is retained. Named or better-documented geometry may replace an anonymous inferred roof only by an explicit later substitution, never by addition to the roof total.
reconciliation_note: Existing structure records include bridges, stockade segments, yards and multi-roof compounds; record count is not roof count. A physical-roof reconciliation precedes the final full-instance release.
reconciled_by: tools/reconcile_665.py — the standing count, the remainder and the block schedule derived from this target are in data/reconstruction/1835_665_roof_programme.json. Every count in THIS file is the authored target and does not move as the town is built — it moves only when evidence retires a slot, which has happened once (see roof_total_note).
